C05-M01-L02-F1.title: Is this authorisation valid for this asset?
C05-M01-L02-F1.caption: A decision graph: only a signatory with legal authority, with every third party accounted for, gives a valid authorisation.
C05-M01-L02-F1.alt: Decision graph. Request to test an asset leads to the decision: Does the signatory own or control it? No leads to Find the right authority (owner or empowered officer), which loops back to the same decision. Yes leads to a second decision: Third party in the path? (cloud, hosting, SaaS, CDN, MSSP). Yes leads to Follow provider policy / get consent, which leads to Valid authorisation (signed and dated before testing); No leads directly to Valid authorisation. Valid authorisation leads to Test within the letter's terms.

nodes.label: Does the signatory own or control it?

C05-M01-L02-F1.note: Only one route reaches testing: through both decisions.

C05-M01-L02-F2.title: Obtaining a valid authorisation: who sends what
C05-M01-L02-F2.caption: The messages between sponsor, testing firm, signatory and third-party provider, in time order, before testing starts.
C05-M01-L02-F2.alt: Sequence diagram with four lanes: Client sponsor, Testing firm, Client signatory, Third-party provider. Sponsor to firm: Request: test the customer portal. Firm to sponsor (reply): Scoping questions + draft scope/RoE. Firm to signatory: Draft letter + annexes. Firm to signatory: Verify authority via known channel. Signatory to firm (reply): Delegation of authority confirmed. Firm to provider: Check provider testing policy. Provider to firm (reply): Conditions / approval. Signatory to firm (reply): Signed, dated letter. Firm to sponsor: Start notice: dates, testers, source IPs.

messages.label: Start notice: dates, testers, source IPs

C05-M01-L02-F2.note: Never start on the sponsor's word alone: the letter comes from the verified signatory.
